SUN: Our own star, and it is quite average
MARS: The red planet, and the god of war
VENUS: Hottest planet, and the goddess of love
EARTH: The only one known to have us on it
URANUS: Ice giant that rolls on its side
NEPTUNE: Furthest planet, and the god of the sea
JUPITER: Biggest planet, with a storm bigger than Earth
MERCURY: Closest to the sun, and a liquid metal
COMET: Dirty snowball that grows a tail near the sun
ORBIT: The path one body takes around another
NEBULA: Cloud of gas and dust where stars are born
GALAXY: Billions of stars bound together, like our Milky Way
QUASAR: Blazing core of a distant young galaxy
PULSAR: Spinning neutron star that ticks like a lighthouse
METEOR: A shooting star, burning up as it falls
ECLIPSE: When one body slides in front of another
ASTEROID: Rocky lump, mostly found in a belt past Mars
COSMOS: Everything there is, taken as a whole
ROCKET: Burns fuel downward to go up
APOLLO: The programme that put boots on the moon
GEMINI: Two-seat NASA programme, and the twins
ORION: The hunter with a famous belt of three stars
TITAN: Saturn's biggest moon, with lakes of methane
EUROPA: Jupiter's icy moon with an ocean beneath
PHOBOS: The larger of Mars's two small moons
DEIMOS: The smaller Martian moon, named for dread
IO: Jupiter's moon, the most volcanic place we know
CERES: Dwarf planet living in the asteroid belt
